settings.question: What is the best blank hoodie for printing?
settings.answer: A mid-weight fleece pullover hoodie is the best all-round blank for printing. The flat chest panel above the kangaroo pocket gives screen printing and DTF a clean surface, the thick fleece keeps prints opaque, and a pullover (versus a zip-up) leaves the front unbroken for a centered design.

settings.question: Can you screen print over a hoodie's kangaroo pocket?
settings.answer: Not cleanly. The pocket opening and the seams beneath it lift the fabric off the platen, so ink lays down unevenly. Keep prints on the flat upper chest above the pocket, or move the design to the full back. A crewneck sweatshirt avoids the issue entirely.

settings.question: Are pullover or zip-up hoodies better for printing?
settings.answer: Pullovers are better for front graphics because the front is one continuous panel — a zipper would split a centered design down the middle. Choose a zip-up only when you're decorating a left-chest logo or a full-back print, which a zipper doesn't interrupt.

settings.question: What weight hoodie is best for printing?
settings.answer: A mid-weight fleece — roughly 8 oz / 280 gsm — is the standard. It's heavy enough to stay opaque and hang well after printing, but not so heavy that it's slow to cure. Lighter triblend hoodies feel softer and more retail, but show ink through less and suit DTF or soft-hand prints.

settings.question: Can you print on dark hoodies?
settings.answer: Yes. For screen printing a dark hoodie, lay down a white underbase first so the colors stay vivid. DTF is the easier route — its film transfer bonds to any color with no separate underbase screen, which is why many shops use it for dark and mixed fleece.

settings.question: Are blank hoodies good for embroidery?
settings.answer: They're one of the best substrates for it. Fleece is thick enough to support dense stitching without puckering, making left-chest logos and back designs look crisp. Hoop the flat chest panel and avoid stitching across the pocket opening; a crewneck sweatshirt is the easiest of all to hoop.
